title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 140-3, 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'). Grothendieck works with a profinite group 𝔖 that has an index-2 subgroup 𝔖^+ and a sign character ε_𝔖 : 𝔖 → 𝔖/𝔖^+ ≅ {±1}. Two distinguished elements ρ, σ lie in 𝔖^+ (on the next page this group is written Ĝ^+). An element ρ acts by conjugation, ρ(α) = ρ α ρ^{-1}. The bracket [α,ρ] = α ρ(α)^{-1} is then the commutator α ρ α^{-1} ρ^{-1}, so [α,ρ]ρ = α ρ α^{-1}. A central procyclic subgroup L_0 = SZ_{ρ,σ} is the image of Ẑ → L_0, n ↦ ε_0^n. A further element ε_1 is used through its 'odd powers' ε_1^{μ-1} for μ ∈ Ẑ*; the underbrace identifies ε_1^{μ-1} with ρ_1^ν, where ν = (μ-1)/2 makes sense because μ is a 2-adic unit. L_1 is the corresponding subgroup.

Section 6°, the set Σ_{ρ,σ} (68). It consists of the 5-tuples (ξ, η, μ, ε', ε) in 𝔖^+ × 𝔖^+ × Ẑ* × {±1} × {±1} such that:
- ξρ is 𝔖^+-conjugate to ρ^{ε'};
- ησ is 𝔖^+-conjugate to σ^{ε};
- ξ = η ε_1^{μ-1}. This is the 'loop equation' linking the two twisting elements.

NB after (68). The data are partly redundant.
- If ρ is not 𝔖^+-conjugate to ρ^{-1}, then ε' is determined by ξ; likewise ε is determined by η when σ is not conjugate to σ^{-1}. The latter forces σ² ≠ 1.
- If n ↦ ε_0^n is injective, μ is determined by (ξ,η). The defining relation then reduces to the membership condition (69): η^{-1}ξ ∈ L_1.

The set SG_{ρ,σ} (70). It is the set of triples (α, β, μ) in 𝔖 × 𝔖 × Ẑ* with [α,ρ] = [β,σ] ε_1^{μ-1}. Here the twisting elements are written as twisted commutators with elements of the big group 𝔖, which may be orientation-reversing.

The map (71), SG_{ρ,σ} → Σ_{ρ,σ}, sends (α,β,μ) to:
- ξ = [α,ρ] and η = [β,σ];
- μ unchanged;
- ε' = ε_𝔖(α) and ε = ε_𝔖(β).

The marginal NB checks that ξ, η lie in 𝔖^+: ε_𝔖(α ρ(α)^{-1}) = 1 because ρ acts trivially on 𝔖/𝔖^+. The map is declared 'évidemment' surjective.

Purpose, as seen on the next page. Σ^ét ⊂ Σ is the set of tuples realised by an automorphism u of Ĝ^+ with u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ησ. Such tuples are in bijection with Grothendieck's group 𝔅_{ρ,σ} of automorphisms that:
- preserve the conjugacy classes of ρ and σ up to inversion;
- act on ε_0 by the character μ.

SG^ét is the inverse image of Σ^ét. The whole page therefore builds a 'set of solutions of the loop equation' (α,β,μ) that surjects onto a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-like automorphism group. It parallels the later description of GT by pairs (λ,f) acting via x ↦ x^λ, y ↦ f^{-1} y^λ f, but here with orientation signs and an extended group 𝔖 ⊃ 𝔖^+. The configuration 'σ not conjugate to σ^{-1}, hence σ² ≠ 1, with a central ε_0' is suggestive of B_3 = ⟨ρ,σ | ρ³ = σ²⟩ or of (profinite) SL_2 / mapping-class-type groups. However, the page itself keeps the setting abstract.
errors: In the NB after (68), the second clause says 'ε′ est déterminé par ξ,η' for the case σ not conjugate to σ^{-1}; logically it should be ε (the sign attached to σ). This is a slip, either in the manuscript or in its reading.
In the margin, ε_𝔖(ξ) is written as 'α ρ(α) = 1'. It should be ε_𝔖(α)·ε_𝔖(ρ(α))^{-1} = 1; this is harmless, since inverses coincide in {±1}.

The map (71) being well defined and 'évidemment' surjective uses unstated hypotheses. (i) Conjugation by any odd element of 𝔖 must send ρ (resp. σ) to an 𝔖^+-conjugate of ρ^{-1} (resp. σ^{-1}). (ii) Surjectivity for ε′ = −1 or ε = −1 requires an odd element that inverts ρ (resp. σ) exactly, e.g. 𝔖 = 𝔖^+ ⋊ ⟨τ⟩ with τρτ^{-1} = ρ^{-1}, τστ^{-1} = σ^{-1}. These presumably hold in Grothendieck's intended example but are not stated on this page.

The statement that, when n ↦ ε_0^n is injective, μ is determined by ξ,η and (69) holds silently uses that μ ↦ ε_1^{μ-1} is injective with image L_1, i.e. a relation between ε_1 and ε_0 fixed on earlier pages.

ideas.what: Parametrising automorphisms that preserve conjugacy classes of two generators up to inversion by 'twisting elements' ξ = [u,ρ], η = [u,σ], subject to a loop equation ξ = η ε_1^{μ-1} with a cyclotomic-type character μ ∈ Ẑ*.
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld/Ihara-style description of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type groups (pairs (λ,f)); inertia-preserving / braid-like automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s); Lochak–Schneps, Harbater–Schneps for B_3 / SL_2-type versions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches the Teichmüller tower and GT idea; this detailed formalism is in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation.

ideas.what: Lifting the twisting data to elements α,β of an orientation-extended group 𝔖 ⊃ 𝔖^+, with the sign character recording whether u inverts the conjugacy classes (ε′, ε).
ideas.modern_name: Extended (orientation-reversing) mapping class / Teichmüller groups; complex conjugation and the GT̂ action on extended braid groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in GT literature (complex conjugation in GT̂; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura)

ideas.what: Membership reformulation η^{-1}ξ ∈ L_1 when the central procyclic subgroup is free (Ẑ → L_0 injective).
ideas.modern_name: Elimination of the cyclotomic parameter when the centre is torsion-free

ideas.what: Surjection SG_{ρ,σ} → Σ_{ρ,σ} and restriction to the 'étale' part SG^ét → Σ^ét ≅ 𝔅_{ρ,σ}.
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of an automorphism group as a quotient of a solution set of commutator equations

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, in the abstract (two elements ρ,σ, a central procyclic subgroup, an index-2 orientation extension), a GT-type parametrisation that incorporates orientation signs (ε′,ε) and the inversion of conjugacy classes. This is a sign-refined variant of the later (λ,f) description, with the 'loop equation' [α,ρ] = [β,σ] ε_1^{μ-1}. It is a documented unpublished precursor rather than a new theorem.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck, around 1981, systematically handling orientation-reversing elements and B_3/SL_2-type central extensions in the GT programme, roughly a decade before Drinfeld's GT. The page contains no result absent from later work.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine set-theoretic bookkeeping inside Grothendieck's unpublished GT-like formalism (signs, central character, twisting commutators). It is historically interesting as a precursor of the (λ,f) description of GT, but it contains no new theorem or connection beyond what the later GT literature developed.
transcription_corrections: In (68) the image appears to show '=' (with '‖' beneath) rather than the transcription's '⊂'. Reading uncertain; logically '⊂' is intended.
In the NB, the image indeed reads 'ε′ est déterminé par ξ,η' in the σ clause; mathematically this should be ε.
Marginal note: 'car on a ε_𝔖(ξ) = ε(α)ρ(α) = 1', with ε_𝔖 applied to α and ρ(α), not the bare product 'α ρ(α)'.
The word struck under the third condition in (68) ('aussi') is crossed out; the underbrace reads 'ρ_1^ν ∴ ν = (μ−1)/2'.
